source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Include the relevant vehicle information such as make, model, year, VIN number, and the date of inspection.
3. Detail the specific test conducted (e.g., brake system inspection, single brake test, or dynamic brake performance test).
4. Clearly state the reason for the failure.
   - Identify which parts of the braking system failed (e.g., broken or missing components, leaks, worn-out brake pads, faulty master cylinder, damaged brake lines, etc.).
   - Specify whether the failure was on a specific wheel (left front, right rear, etc.) or a system-wide issue.
5. Record the test measurements.
   - Document the brake force or pressure applied.
   - Note the effectiveness of the brakes in terms of stopping distance or pedal travel.
   - Include observations such as brake fade, pulling to one side, or pedal pulsation.
6. Provide objective evidence.
   - Take photos or videos (if possible) of the failed
